plan.topic: A pill to prevent GLP-1 vomiting? Tradipitant Phase 3 Study 3601 after a single semaglutide dose (Vanda, Oct 27, 2026)
plan.angle: Hook: 'Can a pill stop GLP-1 vomiting before it starts? A new Phase 3 trial tested one.' Credit: 'Vanda, Oct 27, 2026; company-reported, not peer-reviewed.' Numbers: any vomiting 43.0% (61 of 142) on tradipitant vs 58.5% (96 of 164) on placebo, after one semaglutide dose given without the usual gradual start, so it's a stress test and not how real treatment begins. Status: tradipitant is approved in the US for motion-sickness vomiting, but not for GLP-1 vomiting; Vanda plans to file. No tirzepatide data. Mechanism: it blocks NK-1 signals in the brain's vomiting centre. What helps today: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping at comfortably full, sipping fluids; tell your prescriber about vomiting that keeps going; don't take any anti-sickness medicine for this without your prescriber. 'Not personal advice' plus the prescriber line, with a loop ending. Title: 'Semaglutide Vomiting: Could a Pill Prevent It?'
plan.working_title: Semaglutide Nausea: Could a Pill Prevent the Vomiting?
plan.why: The freshest randomized result on the radar (Oct 27, momentum 88, low competition). It speaks to the top worry of GLP-1 users, but it's too new and press-release-only for a long video. | fact-check: The trial exists and the numbers check out. Vanda press release, 27 Oct 2026: Study 3601, Phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled; any vomiting 43.0% (61/142) vs 58.5% (96/164), p=0.006; all participants got a single 1 mg semaglutide dose without titration; an sNDA is planned; 'generally well tolerated'. Problems: (1) NCT06804603 is the earlier Phase 2 trial (124 enrolled, BMI 25–40, diabetes excluded), not Study 3601. Don't take Study 3601's population from it. The press release doesn't state the population, so say only 'adults given a single semaglutide dose'. (2) Tradipitant (NEREUS) has been FDA-approved since 30 Dec 2025 for preventing motion-sickness vomiting. 'Not approved' is therefore inaccurate. The correct line is 'approved in the US for motion sickness, not for GLP-1 vomiting'. Add 'don't take it or any anti-sickness medicine for this without your prescriber', so the Short doesn't encourage off-label self-use. (3) The hook 'Just started a GLP-1 and the nausea hit?' implies it treats existing nausea in real patients. The trial tested prevention after one untitrated dose, so reframe the hook. (4) Give the relative reduction only next to the absolute numbers. Company-reported, not peer-reviewed. No tirzepatide data. Sources: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vanda-pharmaceuticals-announces-positive-results-from-study-3601-of-nereus-tradipitant-for-prevention-of-glp-1induced-vomiting-302920054.html ; https://www.hcplive.com/view/tradipitant-cuts-semaglutide-induced-vomiting-in-phase-3-trial ; https://www.hcplive.com/view/fda-approves-tradipitant-nereus-for-the-prevention-of-vomiting-induced-by-motion

factcheck.summary:
The facts are correct and the safety lines are there, so this passes, with three small fixes to apply.

I checked every number against Vanda's 27 October 2026 press release (Study 3601) and HCPLive's coverage. They match exactly: any vomiting 43.0% (61 of 142 people) on tradipitant versus 58.5% (96 of 164) on placebo, p=0.006. The trial was Phase 3, randomized and placebo-controlled, using a single 1 mg semaglutide dose with no gradual start. The script already frames that dose as a stress test.

These claims also check out:
- Tradipitant is an NK-1 receptor antagonist that acts in the brain's vomiting centre.
- The FDA approved it on 30 December 2025 for preventing motion-sickness vomiting only.
- Vanda plans to file a supplemental application (sNDA) for GLP-1-induced vomiting.
- The release has no tirzepatide data.
- Wharton 2022 supports saying nausea and vomiting are among the most common side effects, and supports the self-care tips.

Safety is covered: the script says not to take anti-sickness medicine without a prescriber, to tell your prescriber about ongoing vomiting, and includes "Not personal advice" plus the prescriber line.

The three fixes:
1. The narration is about 176 words, over the 170-word Shorts limit.
2. "Not peer-reviewed" should say "not yet peer-reviewed".
3. The script doesn't say what is known about tradipitant's side effects.
